items.detail: **Tuesday's October CPI** is the week's main event, with prices expected to rise **0.3%** on the month and core prices 0.2%.
items.why: A hotter print would firm up a December rate hike and hit the tech stocks behind last week's selloff.

items.detail: **CoreWeave** reports after Tuesday's close and **Cisco** after Thursday's close, the first big checks on AI spending since last week's chip rout.
items.why: Strong spending plans could steady the Nasdaq; weak guidance would add to fears about AI regulation.

items.detail: The **S&P 500** starts at **7,376.86**, with traders putting the odds of a December Fed hike at about 77% after Friday's strong jobs report.
items.why: With hike odds already high, any sign of cooling inflation could spark a relief rally in beaten-down stocks.

items.detail: **China** reports October trade on Tuesday, after Monday's factory-gate inflation hit **5.7%**, a four-year high, while Taiwan and Korea chip stocks stay under heavy pressure.
items.why: A hot US CPI would lift the dollar and add to outflows from Asian chip markets.

items.detail: India's **October CPI** comes out Thursday in a holiday-shortened week, with markets shut Tuesday. The **NIFTY 50** is testing the 25,000–25,200 zone.
items.why: Low inflation and cheaper oil keep foreign buying going; an upside surprise would test the rally.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** starts near **2,754** and sits close to major support, and Tuesday's CPI could decide whether that level holds.
items.why: Small caps are moving closely against Treasury yields, so a hot print that pushes yields up would hurt them most.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** starts near **$75,500**, just above its 200-day average near $73,200, with Tuesday's US CPI the week's main test.
items.why: Spot ETFs lost $1.28 billion last week; higher hike odds could push it below that support.

items.detail: **Ether** slid to about **$2,136** on Monday, its lowest since August, after spot ETFs had six straight weeks of outflows.
items.why: Steady fund selling leaves little support; a soft CPI that cools hike bets is the likeliest turn.

items.detail: **Solana** starts near **$89.65**, testing a long-term trendline after six weekly losses, with no protocol event this week to lean on.
items.why: Solana ETFs keep losing money, and as the most volatile big coin it swings hardest on rate surprises.

items.detail: **Spot gold** starts near **$4,077** ahead of Tuesday's US CPI, which is forecast to rise 0.3% on the month.
items.why: A soft print would weaken the dollar and yields and help gold; a hot one would firm up hike bets.

crossCuttingTheme: Tuesday's US October CPI links every market: a hot print would lock in a December Fed hike and lift the dollar and yields, hurting tech, small caps, crypto and Asian chips, while a soft one would help gold and India.
